subject: spinning asteroid
title: This Asteroid Spins Every 2 Minutes and Should Have Torn Apart

scenes.text: This asteroid spins once every two minutes. It shouldn't exist.
It's about 710 meters wide, spotted in the first images from the new Rubin Observatory.
One full turn takes just 1.88 minutes, a record for an asteroid that big.
Most asteroids are loose rubble piles, held together only by weak gravity.
Spin a rubble pile faster than once every 2.2 hours, and it flings itself apart.
It spins about seventy times faster, so it must be solid rock. Watch it turn again.

description:
Asteroid 2025 MN45, about 710 meters across, completes one rotation every 1.88 minutes, the fastest spin ever measured for an asteroid larger than 500 meters.
It was found in the first data from the Vera C. Rubin Observatory and announced in January 2026 in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.
Main-belt rubble piles break apart if they spin faster than about once every 2.2 hours, so this one needs the strength of solid rock to hold together.
What do you think keeps a mountain of rock spinning that fast in one piece?
first_comment: A day on this asteroid lasts less than two minutes, so you'd see over 700 sunrises in a single Earth day. Would you want to stand on it?
